summaries.summary: Databricks Apps is Databricks' serverless hosting for Python and Node.js apps and the recommended runtime for new agents, Agent Runtime and custom MCP servers, replacing Model Serving. Each app gets a dedicated service principal (App authorization), optionally combined with Public Preview User authorization via a forwarded user token. Endpoints require OAuth, not PATs; permissions are CAN USE and CAN MANAGE. Limits: 100 apps per workspace; compute sizes Medium (0.5 DBU/h, default), Large and XLarge, billed hourly while running.

Databricks Apps user authorization (Public Preview, formerly on-behalf-of-user) lets an app or agent act as the calling user via a downscoped token in the x-forwarded-access-token header. A workspace admin must enable it, and apps declare scopes in user_api_scopes (such as sql, genie, files, model-serving, ai-gateway). Admins control the allowlist via allowedAppsUserApiScopes (an empty array disables it). Scope changes take up to 5 minutes, and existing apps must restart after first enablement.

Databricks automatic identity management syncs users, service principals and groups from the identity provider without SCIM, and Databricks recommends it over SCIM, which remains the fallback. It is GA for Microsoft Entra ID (since 2026-05-26) and Okta (since 2026-07-03, with Okta as source of truth for group memberships). This determines how human and agent identities reach Databricks; JIT provisioning also creates users on first login for supported IdPs.

The Databricks CLI is Databricks' official command-line tool, GA from v1.0.0 (May 2026); the latest release is v1.26.0 (2026-11-11). It signs in with databricks auth login (U2M OAuth tokens last one hour and auto-refresh), keeps profiles in ~/.databrickscfg and tokens in the OS credential store. It covers agent-relevant groups such as apps, bundle, serving-endpoints, genie, vector search and aitools, and is required by the Agent Bricks CLI. On Windows install via winget.

Databricks context-based ingress control (GA since 2026-07-21; account-level policies Beta) lets account admins write allow/deny rules combining identity, request type (UI, API, Apps runtime, Lakebase), source IP, private endpoints and partner platforms. It requires the Enterprise tier, and IP access lists are ANDed with it. Since 2026-11-10, ChatGPT and Claude can be allowed as partner platforms, so hosted MCP clients can connect without tracking their IPs.

The Enterprise tier is Databricks' top pricing tier on AWS and GCP, equivalent to Premium on Azure Databricks. It gates security features agents depend on, including context-based ingress control and serverless network policies. Account admins upgrade to it from the account console Settings.

Foundation Model APIs are Databricks-hosted model endpoints (databricks-* and system.ai.*) serving Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Llama and other models, fronted by Unity Gateway. Billing is pay-per-token in DBUs or provisioned throughput, which Databricks recommends for production. Most models allow 1M ITPM, 100K OTPM and 360K RPH per workspace; requests cap at 4 MB, 200 RPS and 597 s. A 429 means your limit, a 503 Databricks capacity; models retire on short cycles.

The metastore admin is the optional Databricks Unity Catalog role that manages privileges and ownership in a metastore; Databricks recommends assigning it to a group. Workspaces created after 2023-11-08 may have none, with workspace admins getting create privileges instead, but it is still needed to change ownership of objects you don't own. It is needed to manage system.ai (or MANAGE) and, with account admin, to access system tables by default.

Databricks Model Serving hosts custom models and, historically, agents; agents on Model Serving are now legacy, with Databricks recommending Databricks Apps for new agents (no retirement date published). Agents authenticate via automatic passthrough (recommended, deployer permissions), on-behalf-of-user (Public Preview) or manual credentials. Limits include 16 MB payloads (4 MB for agents), 597 s timeout and 200 QPS per workspace without route optimization; GPU endpoints bill DBUs per hour.

Network connectivity configurations (NCCs) are Databricks account-level regional objects, created by account admins and attached to workspaces, that manage serverless private endpoints. Serverless private endpoints are charged per hour and per GB processed, and the legacy serverless stable IP list was decommissioned. Status is unconfirmed: the NCC page calls private connectivity private preview, while release notes say private connectivity to AWS-managed resources went GA on 2026-10-12.

Databricks network policies are account-level serverless egress controls (one per workspace) in Full Access or Restricted Access mode, requiring the Enterprise tier. Restricted Access allows only UC external locations, listed FQDNs, S3 buckets and same-workspace APIs, supports dry-run, and covers notebooks, jobs, SQL warehouses, pipelines, Model Serving and Apps (limited). Agents need external model providers and MCP servers added as allowed destinations; blocking specific destinations is Public Preview since 2026-06-23.

A Databricks OAuth secret is the credential a service principal uses for OAuth M2M, the main way agents authenticate non-interactively. Each service principal can hold up to five secrets valid up to 730 days, shown only once and created by account or workspace admins. Since 2026-08-29 secrets can be restricted to API scopes (fixed at creation; unscoped means all-apis), and since 2026-09-16 unused secrets are auto-deleted after 90 days.

OAuth U2M is Databricks' user-to-machine OAuth flow for interactive users, used by the Databricks CLI and accepted by MCP servers such as Genie One. CLI U2M tokens expire after one hour and are refreshed automatically. On-behalf-of OAuth to Genie One MCP needs the ai-gateway scope. General U2M token and refresh-token lifetimes remain unconfirmed.

On-behalf-of user authorization (Public Preview, now called User authorization) lets a Databricks agent act as the calling user via a downscoped token in x-forwarded-access-token, with scopes like sql, genie and model-serving. Call get_user_workspace_client() inside invoke or stream, not at startup. Missing scopes break get_current_user, and a UUID instead of a username means silent fallback to the app service principal. Apps must restart after first enablement; scope changes take up to 5 minutes.

Databricks personal access tokens (PATs) are legacy, workspace-scoped bearer tokens that can't automate account-level APIs and aren't accepted by Databricks Apps endpoints. New PATs default to a 730-day maximum (Databricks recommends under 90 days), unused tokens are revoked after 90 days, and users can hold up to 600 per workspace. Workspace admins can disable PATs (enabled by default), which may break Partner Connect; management requires Premium or above. API scopes and Preview auto-scoping are supported.

Databricks RBAC assumable roles (GA since 2026-08-19) let a principal act as a group with the Assume permission, applying only the role's permissions, with audit logs recording run_by and run_as. Account admins enable it for the account, then workspace admins per workspace. A service principal or agent gets a role-scoped OAuth token by adding assume_group to a workspace token request; account-level token requests don't support role assumption.

Serverless usage policies (formerly serverless budget policies) are Databricks controls that tag serverless usage for cost attribution, with tags landing in custom_tags of system.billing.usage. They cover notebooks, jobs, Lakeflow pipelines, model serving, Lakebase Autoscaling and Apps, so they matter for attributing agent costs. Workspace admins create them, permissions are User and Manager, and an account-wide view needs Billing admin.

A Databricks service principal is the API-only automation identity and the runtime identity for agents; Databricks has no separate agent identity type. It authenticates with OAuth M2M secrets or workload identity federation; account admins add and assign it to workspaces, with Service principal manager and user roles controlling it. Each Databricks App gets its own non-shareable service principal. Unused OAuth secrets are deleted after 90 days, and role-scoped tokens are available via assume_group.

The Databricks SQL Statement Execution API runs SQL on a warehouse over REST (POST /api/2.0/sql/statements/ plus status, cancel and result-chunk endpoints), and the caller needs CAN USE on the warehouse. wait_timeout is 5-50 s (default 10 s) with CONTINUE or CANCEL on timeout. INLINE results cap at 25 MiB; larger results need EXTERNAL_LINKS presigned URLs, which must not receive the Authorization header, and only the submitting user can fetch results.

Databricks system.ai MCP servers are Databricks-provided managed MCP servers served through Unity Gateway at the workspace /ai-gateway/mcp-services/ path, using the OAuth scope ai-gateway. system.ai.genie_one_mcp is GA, while dbsql, web_search and sandbox are Beta and need an account admin to enable the Enhanced Unity Gateway preview. Connectors moved under Unity Gateway on 2026-08-06, requiring reconnection; web_search is unavailable in HIPAA workspaces.

The Databricks workspace admin manages one workspace's identities and compute and belongs to the reserved admins group. The account admin who creates a workspace becomes its admin; on Azure, subscription Contributor or Owner also grants it on first login. Workspace admins gate agent setup: they enable Apps user authorization and its scope allowlist, enable the Managed MCP Servers preview, can disable PATs, and create serverless usage policies.

Dataverse is Microsoft's Power Platform data store; each environment has zero or one Dataverse database. Agents reach it through the OData Web API, SDKs or the Dataverse MCP server rather than JDBC/ODBC, and since September 2026 its tables are a Copilot Studio knowledge source. Access uses predefined security roles (makers need System Customizer plus Environment Maker). Service protection limits are 6,000 requests and 1,200 s execution per user per 5 minutes, plus 52 concurrent requests.

A Dataverse application user is Microsoft's machine identity for Power Platform data access: an unlicensed Dataverse user bound to one Entra app registration or managed identity and given security roles. It is created in Power Platform admin center under Environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Application users, limited to one per Entra app per environment. Application users bypass environment security groups, so they can run in secured environments without membership.

The Dataverse MCP server is Microsoft's GA MCP endpoint at the org's /api/mcp path, with tools such as search_data, read_query, describe, record and table CRUD, and invoke_api. Claude connects via the local @microsoft/dataverse npm proxy or a custom Entra app granted the mcp.tools permission. Only Copilot Studio is enabled by default; Power Platform admins must allow-list other clients per environment. Usage is billed in Copilot Credits.

Declarative Automation Bundles (renamed from Databricks Asset Bundles on 2026-03-16, non-breaking) define Databricks resources as code in databricks.yml, deployed with databricks bundle. The direct deployment engine is the default and the Terraform engine was removed in CLI 1.20.0. Recent versions add Genie Agent, AI Search and AI Function resources, but custom mcp- apps aren't yet supported. Databricks recommends bundles for jobs and pipelines and Terraform for workspace provisioning.

The Developer Knowledge MCP server is Google's documentation MCP server at developerknowledge.googleapis.com/mcp, covering public Google developer docs including Google Cloud, Firebase, Android and Maps. Its tools are search_documents, get_documents and answer_query. It authenticates with an API key header or OAuth/ADC and is enabled with gcloud services enable. Model Armor prompt-injection filters can cause false-positive 403s; HIGH_AND_ABOVE confidence is recommended.

The Discovery Engine API (discoveryengine.googleapis.com) is Google's REST API behind Agent Search (formerly Vertex AI Search) and programmatic Gemini Enterprise access, including StreamAssist. It authenticates with ADC, gcloud access tokens, attached service accounts, impersonation (needs Service Account Token Creator) or workload identity federation. ADK and A2A agents are registered in Gemini Enterprise via its v1alpha agents.create endpoint, which requires the Gemini Enterprise Admin role.

Document AI was Snowflake's document extraction feature; its UI and the model PREDICT method were decommissioned on 2026-03-16. AI_EXTRACT replaces it, including for legacy models migrated to the Snowflake Model Registry, while unmigrated models are unavailable. Agents doing document extraction on Snowflake should use AI_EXTRACT.

The Einstein Trust Layer is Salesforce's security layer for generative AI and Agentforce, including MCP tools. It enforces zero data retention with external LLM partners such as OpenAI and Azure OpenAI, masks PII before prompts leave Salesforce (except when an agent action calls a prompt template), and adds dynamic grounding, toxicity detection, prompt defense and an audit trail in Data 360. Whether zero retention covers all bring-your-own models is unconfirmed.

EPM Agent Skills are Oracle's packaged Agent Skills-standard skills that let third-party agents such as Claude and ChatGPT/Codex work with Cloud EPM; Oracle chose skills, not MCP, for this. A root router dispatches to Auth, Core (11 admin skills) and Platform folders, backed by 22 OpenAPI YAML files. Authentication is Basic only, from a private config file, so MFA accounts can't use it. Skills need Python 3.10+ (some Node.js) and EPM Enterprise; since 26.11 the download requires a business process.

EPM Assistants are Oracle's GenAI agent teams for Cloud EPM built in Fusion AI Agent Studio, calling Cloud EPM REST APIs scoped to each user's EPM roles. They need a separate AI Agent Studio entitlement and use its LLMs; whether EPM-only customers can get it is unconfirmed. They are downloaded as zips (only for EPCM, FreeForm and Planning with AI enabled), imported as supervisor agents, tested and published. The catalog spans ARCS, EPCM, FCCS, Narrative Reporting and more.

EPM Automate is Oracle's official Cloud EPM CLI for data, job, snapshot, user and file operations. It supports Basic auth and recommended OAuth 2 via encrypted .epw files, but user and role commands require Basic, Basic can't use SSO or MFA, and most commands need Service Administrator. From 26.12 only the new .epw format (26.09+ clients) works. On Windows it installs from an environment's Downloads, with data under ProgramData; JDK 17 is deprecated in 27.01.

EPM Enterprise is Oracle's full-suite Cloud EPM tier, including multiple cubes, Groovy, Transaction Matching, Tax Provisions, EPCM and all AI and GenAI features. AI capabilities, including EPM Agent Skills, are EPM Enterprise only. Advisers (unverified) report pricing per hosted named user (about USD 500 per month, 25-user minimum) or per hosted employee per month.

The EPM Integration Agent is Oracle's official Cloud EPM client (EPMAgent.zip, a Java process or Windows service) that queries on-premises sources or runs scripts and loads results into Cloud EPM, with write-back adapters. It runs synchronously via a web gateway or asynchronously by polling, grouped into clusters. It signs in as a native non-SSO admin with an encrypted password, optionally an OAuth client ID, configured in agentparams.ini; keep a pre-26.08 .epw until the agent is on 26.10.

A Foundry agent is an agent in Microsoft Azure AI Foundry; each new agent gets a unique blueprint and default agent identity starting with no resource permissions, while legacy agents share a project identity that changes on migration. Agents get implicit model inference and session storage access via the project endpoint. Publishing agents or granting Foundry User to agent identities needs Foundry Project Manager; agent scope is a narrower RBAC scope, and a narrow custom role is the least-privilege option.

Foundry Agent Service is Microsoft's GA managed agent platform in Azure AI Foundry, offering prompt, voice (preview) and hosted agent types and replacing the Assistants API with Responses-based agents. It supports Entra auth only (no API keys), built-in tools including MCP, OpenAPI and A2A (v1.0 GA; unversioned requests default to v0.3), and network isolation via a delegated subnet. Fixed limits include 128 tools per agent and 1,000 versions; agents themselves are free, with tokens and tools billed.

Standard setup is the Foundry Agent Service mode that stores agent data in customer-owned resources: files in Azure Storage, vector stores in Azure AI Search and conversations and metadata in Cosmos DB for NoSQL (at least 3000 RU/s); basic setup uses Microsoft-managed resources. The project managed identity needs Cosmos DB Operator, Storage Account Contributor, Search Index Data Contributor, Search Service Contributor, blob data roles on two containers and Cosmos DB Built-in Data Contributor on enterprise_memory.

Foundry deployment types are Microsoft's model deployment SKUs (GlobalStandard, DataZoneStandard, Standard, provisioned, batch and DeveloperTier) that determine where prompts are processed: any region for Global, a data zone such as US or EU for DataZone, the resource geography for Standard. Data at rest stays in the customer geography, and Azure Policy on the SKU name can enforce residency. New models arrive Global first; Batch costs 50% less with 24-hour turnaround, and Developer tier expires after 24 hours.

Foundry hosted agents run your own agent code (Agent Framework, LangGraph, OpenAI or Anthropic SDKs, Python or C#) in Microsoft Foundry per-session VM-isolated sandboxes, each with a dedicated Entra agent identity and endpoint exposing Responses, Invocations, Activity and A2A. Setup needs ACR and Log Analytics roles that only Owner-level admins can assign. Sandboxes go up to 2 vCPU/4 GiB, versions are immutable, sessions cap at 1,000-2,000 per region, and GA status is unconfirmed.

Foundry hub-based projects are Microsoft's legacy, Azure Machine Learning-based project type, shown only in the Foundry (classic) portal. Some catalog models, such as Mixtral-8x22B and tsuzumi-7b, still require them, and the Azure AI Developer role applies only to hubs and AML workspaces. No end-of-life date for hubs or that role has been found.

The Foundry MCP tool lets Microsoft Foundry agents call remote MCP servers, configured with server_url, server_label, allowed_tools, require_approval (default always) and an optional project connection for credentials. Approvals flow via mcp_approval_request and mcp_approval_response. Only remote endpoints work, so stdio servers must be hosted on Container Apps or Functions; private servers need Standard Agent Setup with BYO VNet. Non-streaming calls time out after 100 seconds.

summaries.key: foundry models from partners and community
summaries.summary: Foundry Models from partners and community, such as Anthropic Claude and Cohere, are Azure Marketplace offers classed as Non-Microsoft Products. Subscribing needs Marketplace and SaaS permissions on the subscription and resource group, covered by Owner or Contributor. Student, Visual Studio Enterprise, free-credit and CSP subscriptions can't purchase them, which matters when choosing where to run Claude-based agents on Azure.

Foundry Models sold by Azure are models, including Azure OpenAI and the GPT-6 family, that Microsoft sells directly with Azure deployments, regions and auth. Prompts, completions and training data aren't shared with OpenAI or other providers or used to train models without permission. Billing is per 1M tokens on Standard types, per PTU on provisioned types, and 50% off for Batch with a 24-hour target.

Foundry Project Manager (renamed from Azure AI Project Manager, same role ID) is the Azure RBAC role for creating Foundry projects, building in them and publishing agents. It is the minimum role to publish agents and can assign only Foundry User (ABAC-constrained), for example to new agent identities. It cannot create the ACR and Log Analytics role assignments hosted agents need.

Foundry toolboxes are Microsoft Foundry bundles of tools behind one managed MCP-compatible endpoint, at the project's /toolboxes/{name}/mcp path, usable by any MCP client. They add versioning and promotion, centralized auth, tool_search and call_tool meta-tools for large tool sets, and Skills (preview). Grounding with Bing, computer use, image generation, SharePoint, Fabric data agent and Azure Functions tools can't be placed in a toolbox.

Foundry tracing is Microsoft Foundry's agent observability, built on OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions with integrations for Agent Framework, LangChain, LangGraph and the OpenAI Agents SDK. Traces are stored in Application Insights, and viewing them requires a Log Analytics reader role. It is GA for prompt and hosted agents and in preview for workflow and external agents.
